issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object and adds a StudentCount class. This creates a structural mismatch: students guided by the UML will expect an int return type, while the reference solution uses a custom wrapper type not mentioned in the specification or template. This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected method signature and how other methods (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents, getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) should use the total count.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove or make StudentCount unnecessary), updating getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() to use that int; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and mention the StudentCount helper class in the specification and template so students know to implement or use it. Prefer option A to match the current UML which expects an int.

issues.description: The concept 'total number of students' is presented in the problem statement and UML as an int-returning value (getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int), and the template's TODO points students to implement that method accordingly. The solution, however, represents the same concept with a new type named StudentCount and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object. This introduces a different identifier (StudentCount) for the same conceptual entity and a different API contract, which will confuse students mapping the UML/problem requirements to the provided solution or expected implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the 'total number of students' across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove StudentCount) to match the UML and template instructions, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to specify StudentCount as the return type and document the StudentCount class so students understand the intended type. Prefer option A to minimize cognitive load and keep the API simple for this exercise.
